However, existing methods are typically tailored to specific subjects and tasks, with direct neural-to-kinematic mappings that can entangle subject-specific neural variability with task-dependent motion patterns, limiting generalization. To address these limitations, we introduce AMRT, a shared neural decoding framework for heterogeneous electrode configurations and movement paradigms. Motivated by cortical encoding of movement direction and speed, AMRT adopts a two-stage design that anchors local motion through velocity estimation and refines the resulting trajectories over longer horizons, encouraging reuse of local motion tendencies across subjects and tasks. Across three datasets, AMRT generalizes to unseen trials and subjects and demonstrates transfer potential across neural recordings and movement paradigms, highlighting the potential of shared neural representations and anchor-and-refine decoding for generalizable continuous neural control.

papers.title: Why Cassini's Oval Could Not Replace Kepler's Ellipse?
papers.abstract: In the later seventeenth century, Kepler's ellipse was not yet accepted. Ward claimed that Boulliau's conic hypothesis amounted to a Ptolemaic equant at the ellipse's empty focus, and built his own model on it. Around 1675--1680, Giovanni Domenico Cassini proposed another curve, the ``oval'', a genus-1 quartic with no closed-form Kepler equation; yet its eccentric anomaly shares exactly the leading coefficient of Kepler's, and its empty focus is, for the Sun, 38 times closer to a true equant than the ellipse's. Dynamically, Binet's formula shows that the force producing the oval under the area law departs from the inverse square by an index $\mathcal{D}(e)\sim3/(4e^2)$, depending on the oval's parameter $e$: no single exponent serves the whole family. This absence of universality, not of an area law, distinguishes it from the ellipse, and arguably explains why Cassini, the Académie and Leibniz kept the question open after the \emph{Principia} (1687).

papers.title: Video recordings and play behaviour annotations of group-housed dairy calves on two Dutch farms
papers.abstract: Play is used as an indicator of positive welfare in dairy calves, but openly available video of group-housed calves with individual behaviour annotations is scarce. We describe video from four camera deployments of about one week each in group pens of dairy calves on two farms in the Netherlands: a research and teaching dairy farm (2024 and 2025) and a commercial dairy farm (2024). The recordings comprise 1,173 video files spanning 651 h. For eight observation days, trained observers coded calf behaviour continuously in Noldus The Observer XT with an 18-item ethogram of play and other behaviours, covering 104 h of video, 90 h of which have every calf in the pen coded. The release also contains 1.1 million decoded frames from seven annotated sessions, a per-frame timestamp read by optical character recognition from the camera clock burned into each frame, per-calf segmentation tracks and per-calf frame-level play labels. The data support studies of calf behaviour and welfare and the development and evaluation of automated behaviour recognition.

papers.title: On the origin of Milky Way binary black holes with LISA
papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) may constitute a fraction of dark matter, but distinguishing them from black holes of stellar origin remains a major challenge. We propose a new method based on the three-dimensional localization of Galactic Binary Black Holes (BBHs) by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). While stellar-origin BBHs are expected to be associated with the stellar distribution of the Milky Way, PBHs may trace its more extended dark matter halo. We introduce a spatial overlap ratio that compares the gravitational-wave localization of each binary with the normalized stellar and dark matter density profiles. Using a Fisher-matrix forecast and 1000 Monte Carlo realizations of a 10-year LISA mission, we find that detecting three BBHs with an overlap ratio ln B < 0 occurs in approximately 99% of simulations where BBHs trace dark matter, but in fewer than 0.1% of simulations where they follow the stellar distribution, even when including a stellar halo containing 3% of the Galactic stellar mass. These results suggest that the localization of only a few Galactic BBHs could provide strong evidence for a primordial population, offering an independent test of their possible contribution to dark matter.

papers.title: Generating a simple silicon detector simulation with an open-weight large language model
papers.abstract: Recent LLM developments have seen AI-generated code become commonplace in the software development industry. Without tool access, LLMs cannot execute simulations, and their knowledge of toolkits such as Geant4 is limited. We demonstrate here, a detector simulation workflow with a Qwen3.6-27B model with Q4_K_M GGUF quantisation together with custom resources and tools served via MCP servers to generate a particle detector simulation. In 50 independent runs, 42(29--56)% at 95% CI produced energy-deposit distributions statistically consistent with a reference simulation, measured against a reference simulation. These results provide a proof of concept that MC simulations can be generated using text-based prompts with an LLM, given the necessary resources and tools. More extensive resources, such as example code and additional documentation, are likely to be required for more complex simulation tasks.

papers.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
papers.abstract: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

papers.title: Fourier--Stieltjes palettes on compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exact Rajchman realization. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. This gives a negative answer to an open-range absolute-continuity question of Ohrysko and Wojciechowski.

papers.title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
papers.abstract: Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging. We investigate how engineering the Hilbert-space geometry controls quantum annealing in a family of blockaded-chain models motivated by these encodings. While boundary terms encode the target maximum independent set problem, the bulk geometry induces an auxiliary optimization problem associated with independent sets of cliques. Spectrally, the energetics of the quantum system can be approximated by physically derived clique weights. When the target problem and the auxiliary problems are consistent, the low-energy modes lie predominantly within the target subspace. This spectral structure motivates a diabatic annealing strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states, as tested on the diamond-chain graph family. These results provide a framework for predicting annealing bottlenecks, and demonstrate Hilbert-space engineering as a strategy for improving neutral-atom quantum optimization protocols.

papers.title: No Supersoft X-rays Before SN 2026ahvu: Constraints on a Potentially Prompt Type Ia Progenitor
papers.abstract: The nearby Type Ia supernova SN 2026ahvu offers a rare opportunity to probe its progenitor that may have evolved unusually rapidly. If the progenitor formed in either of the two young stellar clusters near the explosion site in NGC 1433, the delay from star formation to explosion could have been $\sim$100 Myr or less. The distance to NGC 1433 remains uncertain, with published estimates of 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc. Our preliminary fit to the rising ATLAS light curve yields a distance of $17.7^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Mpc. In the classical single-degenerate scenario, a white dwarf steadily burning hydrogen accreted from a non-degenerate companion can emit detectable supersoft X-rays before explosion. We search for this emission using two archival Chandra observations obtained before the explosion. The observations provide a combined exposure of 95.3 ks, with no 0.3-7 keV photons detected within 2" of the supernova position. For a 100 eV blackbody with Galactic foreground absorption, the 95\% bolometric luminosity limits are $6.3\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and $2.7\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc, respectively. At both distances, the observations exclude a hot, compact white dwarf undergoing steady hydrogen burning if the absorption is limited to the Galactic foreground. However, cooler, expanded, or more heavily absorbed photospheres remain viable. Together with the pre-explosion non-detections for SN 2011fe and SN 2014J, our results reinforce the absence of luminous supersoft progenitors in nearby SNe Ia. This pattern is naturally consistent with double-degenerate explosions, although X-ray-faint single-degenerate configurations remain viable. Post-explosion X-ray observations can test for circumstellar interaction and help determine whether material around the progenitor could have obscured a luminous nuclear burning white dwarf.

papers.title: Toeplitz coefficients and the Lu-Tian correspondence on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact embeddable strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold with Reeb field $T$ and Szeg\H o projection $Π$. Herrmann, Hsiao, Marinescu and the second author showed, for any volume form, that the semi-classical cut-offs $χ(k^{-1}ΠPΠ)$ of first-order elliptic self-adjoint Toeplitz operators have full asymptotic expansions. For $P=-\sqrt{-1}T$ and $T$-invariant volume forms, Chang, Herrmann and Hsiao showed that the diagonal coefficients are $a_{j}\intχ(t)t^{n-j}dt$ with local invariants $a_{j}$, computed $a_{0}$ and $a_{1}$, and used normal forms in the Sasakian case. We add one step: on a compact Sasakian manifold, regular or not, $a_{j}=a_{j}(g^{T})/(2π^{n+1})$, where $a_{j}(\cdot)$ is the universal Bergman kernel polynomial and $g^{T}$ the transverse Kähler metric; no line bundle on $X$ is needed. This gives an exact correspondence: the logarithmic term of the Szeg\H o kernel vanishes to infinite order over an open set if and only if $a_{j}(g^{T})=0$ there for all $j\ge n+1$, which for circle bundles is a local form of the theorem of Lu and Tian with its converse. For $(n,0)$-forms on complete Sasakian manifolds, a cut-off by the self-adjoint generator of the Reeb flow, which avoids the self-adjointness question for the Toeplitz operator, gives the same results with twisted coefficients.

papers.title: TEMPO: Regime-Aware Operator Learning with Locally Adapted POD Bases
papers.abstract: Operator learning approximates the solution map of a parametric partial differential equation from data, enabling fast prediction at new parameter values without repeated simulation. The dominant approach fits a single global low-rank basis, typically a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), to all solution snapshots. This fails when the snapshots span qualitatively different solution shapes, from smooth diffusive profiles to near-discontinuous shocks. We propose TEMPO (Trajectory Expectation-Maximization Mixture of POD Operators), a two-phase framework for regime-aware operator learning. In the offline phase, TEMPO recovers latent regimes via expectation-maximization, fitting a dedicated linear or nonlinear basis to each discovered regime. In the online phase, a gating network and per-regime branch networks are trained jointly, routing new inputs to the regimes at inference. We test TEMPO on Burgers' flow, Sod shock tubes, Coanda flow, Darcy flow, Navier-Stokes flow and the heterogeneous Helmholtz equation. With 64 total POD modes, TEMPO gives 18.61% test error on Burgers', compared with 19.61% for global POD. It also gives lower errors on Coanda and Helmholtz.

papers.title: Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
papers.abstract: The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{σ(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{σ(d)}\}$, $σ\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $λ_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_iλ_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $λ_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds. For three, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$ arises, in the optimal dimension $Θ(\log|G|)$, as the residue group of a simplex facet whose $|G|-1$ nonzero box points are Hilbert basis elements of the whole cone; $k$ times such a point is a sum of vertices exactly when its order in $G$ divides $k$. Isolating this arithmetic is costly: if a simplex face has a single Hilbert basis element $h$ that is not a vertex, then $kh$ is a sum of vertices exactly when some $q$ divides $k$, and $d\ge3q-2$, attained for every $q\ge3$; we also find the least dimension for each $G$ with the fewest such elements. Without isolation, every nonzero submonoid of $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ omitting $1$ is $\{k\ge0:kh$ is a sum of vertices$\}$ for a Hilbert basis element $h$ of degree three. For every $0/1$ polytope with $N$ vertices in $\mathbb{R}^r$, three staircase simplices in dimension $O(N(r+1))$ have a face that has IDP exactly when the polytope does. Deciding whether a lattice point $h$ is a sum of vertices is strongly NP-complete, even given vertex expressions of $2h$ and $3h$, and recognizing IDP of a designated facet is coNP-complete; for the whole hull, IDP can first fail in degree linear in $d$, and it holds whenever $d\le5$. For a family of triples defined by words over three letters, we determine the entire Hilbert basis and characterize IDP by two forbidden subsequences.

papers.title: Harmonic-Constrained Hosting Capacity of Active Distribution Networks Using ESS Compensation and Certified Adaptive Decision-Tree Envelopes
papers.abstract: Active distribution networks increasingly rely on coordinated inverter-based resources to accommodate renewable generation, while harmonic limits constrain the capacity that can be connected. This paper proposes a harmonic optimal power flow (HOPF) method with active energy-storage-system (ESS) support. ESS charging, discharging and harmonic-current compensation are jointly scheduled under state-of-charge dynamics and a shared converter-current rating. An adaptive decision tree learns voltage-current partitions from OPF operating points. Within each leaf, an affine plane is fitted on an analytic grid and certified as a lower envelope. A disaggregated mixed-integer formulation embeds these envelopes in a second-order-cone-relaxed network model. Annual hourly data are assessed through daily capacity optimization, followed by componentwise capacity aggregation and chronological full-year feasibility validation. In the case study, the OPF reference of 65.572 MW exceeds the adopted harmonic bounds, whereas HOPF without harmonic support yields an annually validated capacity of 56.892 MW. With each generator capacity bounded by its OPF reference, the proposed method recovers the complete reference allocation. Coordinated energy dispatch and harmonic compensation thus recover generation capacity within the installed ESS converter ratings.

papers.title: On the blow-up of the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two
papers.abstract: We establish three-term asymptotics for the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two as $γ\to 0$ and identify, up to rescaling and symmetries, the profile of the asymptotically worst potential. The proof uses the well-known relation between the one-particle constant and an integral moment of optimizers of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Through the optimizers' characterization as positive, vanishing solutions of the nonlinear elliptic equation $-ΔQ + Q = Q^{s}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the essence of the proof lies in the asymptotic analysis of solutions $Q$ as $s\to\infty$.

papers.title: Representational Change Under Self-Consuming Training: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly exposed to model-generated text, raising the possibility that future models will be trained recursively on the outputs of their predecessors. Prior work on such self-consuming training loops has largely focused on output quality and downstream performance, leaving their effects on internal representations poorly understood. We study how representations evolve across five generations of self-consumption and whether sparse autoencoders (SAEs) remain reliable under this shift. At each generation, we compare a lineage trained on synthetic data with a matched control trained on real data under the same training settings. We evaluate how well SAEs trained before self-consumption transfer to later generations, measuring reconstruction and sparsity across SAE widths, architectures, and model layers. We then fine-tune the original SAE on each generation and use sparse probing to test whether task-relevant information remains concentrated in a small number of latents or becomes more distributed across the representation. We find that zero-shot SAE performance degrades progressively under self-consumption, with growing reconstruction and sparsity gaps that vary substantially across layers. Fine-tuning largely restores reconstruction, but not feature-level usefulness: task-relevant information remains accessible in the full latent space while becoming less concentrated in individual features. These results show that self-consumption induces representational drift and that reconstruction fidelity alone is insufficient to establish that an adapted SAE remains equally useful for interpretation.

papers.title: Catalytic compression of classical communication in exact entanglement transformations
papers.abstract: Entanglement catalysis is usually associated with making otherwise impossible transformations possible. Here we show that it can also change how much classical communication a transformation requires. A catalyst, returned exactly and uncorrelated with the output, can reduce the message alphabet size required for exact transformations of bipartite pure states by a factor that grows without bound as the Schmidt rank increases. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, however, this advantage disappears at the level of the leading communication rate: the optimal catalytic and noncatalytic rates coincide. We characterize the optimal catalytic cost in terms of Rényi entropies, revealing how the entanglement structure of the source and target governs the finite-copy advantage. Our results establish reusable entanglement as a resource for compressing classical communication in quantum state manipulation.

papers.title: Unexpected Plateau: The Constant $ \rm \log ε(Th/Eu)$ Ratio of Actinide-Boost Stars
papers.abstract: The astrophysical site of the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) is still one of the major open questions in astronomy. A key mystery is the origin of the peculiar actinide-to-lanthanide ratio found in the so called actinide-boost stars, with $ \rm \log ε(Th/Eu)>-0.35$. Here we present the largest sample of Th measurements in stars formed in an external galaxy, Gaia Sausage Enceladus. From this sample, we present the three most metal-rich actinide-boost stars discovered to date, $\rm -1.6<[Fe/H]<-1.1$. In addition, we measured Th in a comparison sample of Milky Way stars formed in situ, and compiled Th measurements from the literature which do not account for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) effects. After applying NLTE corrections to the combined sample, a bimodality in the $\rm\logε(Th/Eu)$ ratio is revealed. Unexpectedly, actinide-boost stars lie on a very narrow $(σ=0.02)$ plateau of $\rm \logε(Th/Eu)=-0.2$, clearly separated from actinide-normal stars. Most (if not all) of the actinide-boost stars in our sample originate from outside the Milky Way. Chemical evolution models show that such a plateau can arise, even at [Fe/H] = $-$1, when a single actinide-rich event dominates the r-process content of a small or gas-depleted system. Combined with other evidence, our results suggest that mergers with neutron stars are the most promising astrophysical site for actinide-boost stars.

papers.title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
papers.abstract: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel. Furthermore, we show that the scaling of the low-wave-vector region of the correlation function can accurately reproduce a specified hyperuniform exponent, independently of the structural properties at larger wave numbers. Our results establish a free-energy-based framework for describing disordered hyperuniform states, demonstrating and enabling independent control over structural selection and long-wavelength density correlations.

papers.title: Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion for Decomposable Generative Models
papers.abstract: Generative model pre-training typically optimizes a model as a whole without explicitly organizing its parameters for selective reuse. Decomposable pre-training instead learns reusable components for downstream adaptation while retaining strong generative performance. However, existing knowledge diversion methods incur substantial parameter overhead through weight factorization and rely on fixed component assignments to induce specialization, potentially compromising in-distribution generation quality. We therefore propose Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion (SGKDiv), which learns how generative knowledge is shared and specialized for effective generation and selective downstream reuse. SGKDiv constructs Knowledge Units from paired feed-forward channels, preserving native computational structure without SVD-based reparameterization. Calibrated condition-wise routing combines a shared usage prior with conditional adjustments, while complementary regularization shapes their allocation, diversity, and magnitude. Together, these designs replace predefined component assignments with adaptively learned and explicitly regulated knowledge specialization. Experiments across diverse model and training settings demonstrate better in-distribution generation than dense and MoE baselines, alongside stronger downstream adaptation than representative PEFT methods across eight datasets.

papers.title: An Adaptive Reduced Speed of Light Approximation
papers.abstract: The reduced speed of light approximation (RSLA) is a common approach in radiation-hydrodynamic (RHD) simulations of non-relativistic systems where the gas speed $v_{\rm gas} \ll c$. In the RSLA one eases the severe time step constraint imposed by the speed of light $c$ by replacing it with a reduced value $\hat{c}$ chosen so that $v_{\rm gas} \ll \hat{c} \ll c$. This approach works well in flows with low or moderate optical depth, but fails in optically thick media, where it makes thermal relaxation too slow and gives incorrect RHD wave modes. Here we propose an Adaptive Reduced Speed of Light Approximation (ARSA) that removes these problems by replacing the global speed reduction factor $φ_0 \equiv \hat{c}/c$ with a local, cell-by-cell reduction factor $φ$ derived from a von Neumann stability analysis of the implicit-explicit update used by modern two-moment RHD codes. The resulting limiter has no tunable parameters, can be computed using only local operations, and improves on the classic RSLA by allowing $φ\to 1$ in cells where a reduced speed of light is not required because the exchange with the gas damps unstable modes, allowing recovery of the correct thermal relaxation and wave-damping rates in highly-opaque regions. We compare ARSA to the classic RSLA in a range of standard RHD test problems, and show that in opaque regions where gas holds most of the heat capacity the ARSA is much more accurate than the RSLA at the same time step, or that it can achieve the same accuracy as the RSLA with up to 100 times fewer time steps. However, gains are limited in regions where radiation holds a large share of the heat capacity, as it does in some astrophysical systems.

papers.title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

papers.title: Critical curves and throat degeneracy in black bounces
papers.abstract: Identical critical curves need not imply identical null-orbit dynamics. For a class of static spherical areal-radius deformations, we show that a surviving original photon sphere retains its critical impact parameter and orbital frequency, while its coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent is multiplied by the radial Jacobian. The logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient acquires the inverse factor. At a reflection-symmetric throat, stability factorizes into a derivative of the original optical potential and the throat curvature. More generally, an order-$m$ extremum of the original potential composed with an order-$q$ areal-radius minimum produces an optical degeneracy of order $p=mq$, with critical approach $|x|\propto|t|^{-2/(p-2)}$ and reflected strong deflection $Δφ\propto(b/b_{\rm c}-1)^{-(p-2)/(2p)}$ for $p>2$. For the Simpson--Visser family with mass $M$ and bounce parameter $a$, the critical impact parameter remains Schwarzschild-like for $a<3M$, although the instability varies with $a$. The merger at $a=3M$ is quartic, separating stable and unstable throat branches. These results isolate the null-orbit information preserved by a radial deformation from that encoded in its local geometry.

papers.title: The Stability of the Higgs vacuum inside a Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: I investigate the behaviour of the Higgs field inside a Schwarzschild black hole, including a Planck-suppressed coupling between the Higgs field and the Kretschmann scalar, the leading curvature invariant in a Ricci-flat geometry. Because the radial coordinate is timelike in the interior, the Higgs condensate evolves in time rather than tracking the minimum of its potential. Near the singularity the interior field equation reduces to Bessel's equation, with solution $H=vJ_0(x)$, where $x\propto\sqrtξ\,t_p/τ$ and $τ$ is the proper time to the singularity. Contrary to static analyses, the field remains frozen in its broken phase while the potential changes shape, departing from its vacuum value only when the curvature becomes Planckian, independently of the black-hole mass. Including the one-loop correction from Higgs vacuum fluctuations yields the same Bessel equation with a source term, which I solve exactly; the condensate is reduced by at most about ten per cent. The electroweak symmetry therefore remains broken throughout the interior within the regime of validity of effective field theory.

papers.title: Accessing Electrode Edges: Upright Mounting for Site-Specific Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Cryogenic atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) is increasingly being used to map the three-dimensional distribution of highly reactive species in heterogeneous materials, including those found in battery systems. However, site-specific preparation of localised features and liquid-solid interfaces remains challenging, particularly when regions of interest (ROIs) are concentrated along electrode edges that are difficult to access using conventional mounting geometries. Here, we present a cryo-APT workflow incorporating an upright-mounting procedure that enables targeted specimen preparation of localised regions using plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) microscopy and milling under cryogenic conditions. We first demonstrate the approach using an electrolyte-wetted graphite electrode, successfully preparing and analysing a specimen containing both an edge-localised electrolyte deposit and the underlying graphite and Cu current collector. We then apply the workflow to a cycled graphite electrode, targeting Li dendrites concentrated around the electrode perimeter and successfully preparing and analysing the targeted Li-rich region. Beyond battery systems, this approach offers potential for site-specific cryo-APT of edge-localised features across a broader range of material systems, where conventional specimen preparation geometries may limit access to ROIs.

papers.title: From very fine Vertical Resolution to Range Super-Resolution on BIOMASS P-BAND SAR Data
papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates range super-resolution over arid regions using SAR tomography data with very fine vertical resolution from the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission. As the first civilian spaceborne P-band SAR mission, BIOMASS is operating with a bandwidth limited to 6~MHz by International Telecommunication Union regulations, yielding a native slant-range resolution of approximately 25 m. The large spatial baseline data acquired during the commissioning phase in July and August 2025 provide a valuable opportunity to enhance range resolution based on the InSAR wavenumber shift principle. According to this principle, a wider effective bandwidth can be synthesized by combining complementary sub-bands of the ground reflectivity spectrum sampled across acquisitions at different look angles. Unlike existing literature, this paper offers a novel interpretation of this problem from the perspective of SAR tomography. Furthermore, the proposed method also accounts for residual topography errors. The range resolution enhancement performance is validated using all 20 available acquisitions from the July-August 2025 commissioning phase over Lop Nur, China, and Wadi al-Hayat, Libya, achieving spatial detail comparable to optical satellite imagery in a grid finer than 2 m. Furthermore, the reconstructed range spectrum of the central Libyan oasis exhibits an effective bandwidth exceeding 70 MHz. The point spread function (PSF) of a point like target in the scene demonstrates a slant-range resolution finer than 2.1 m, representing more than a twelvefold improvement over the native resolution.

papers.title: K-out-of-N Oblivious Transfer over Erasure Channels: Capacity and Reductions
papers.abstract: We study $K$-out-of-$N$ oblivious transfer (OT) between a server and a client over a discrete memoryless channel, under an honest-but-curious model. The client must retrieve $K$ out of $N$ messages stored by the server while learning nothing about the remaining $N-K$ messages, and the server must not learn the client's selection. For a binary erasure channel (BEC) with parameter $ε$, we show that the $K$-out-of-$N$ OT capacity is $\min\Big(\frac{Kε}{N-K},1-ε\Big)$. This characterization generalizes the known capacity results for $1$-out-of-$2$ OT and for $1$-out-of-$N$ OT when $ε\ge\tfrac{N-1}{N}$. We also investigate OT reductions, specifically, we show that constructing a $K$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol from repeating $K$ times an optimal $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be suboptimal, but we also identify certain ranges of $ε$ and $M < N$ for which a $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be optimally realized via the repetition of a $1$-out-of-$M$ OT protocol. Finally, we discuss extensions of our results to a generalized erasure channel (GEC).

papers.title: Sequential strategy for depolarizing strength estimation
papers.abstract: We study the advantages of applying a sequential strategy for enhancing the precision in estimating the strength $p$ of a depolarizing channel, using qudit and two-qubit probes. The sequential strategy requires that the same depolarizing channel is repeatedly applied $M$ times to the quantum probe. From the analysis of the probe's output state, both the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and its regularization RQFI, given from multiplication by $p$, are analyzed. We determine that in the limit of $p \to 0$, the QFI is {\it linearly amplified} with the number of channel repetitions. Instead, in the weak-noise regime, the QFI is maximized at a finite value of $M$. Then, the RQFI decreases more quickly with $p$ as $M$ increases. In particular, for two-qubit probes, the RQFI decreases with the depolarization strength proportionally to the amount of correlation between the qubits. The greater the number of channel repetitions, the wider the range of $p$ for which the initial state of the probe that allows for the maximization of the QFI is a separable state. We also show that a single qubit probe undergoing a sequential encoding protocol outperforms the optimal two-qubit single-round QFI for $M>3$ in the weak-noise regime.

papers.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
papers.abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

papers.title: What You Post Is What You Symptom: Estimating Psychometric Networks from Social Media Discourse
papers.abstract: Symptom networks in psychopathology are estimated almost exclusively from self-report questionnaires, restricting inference to whatever symptom set a given instrument covers. We introduce a framework for symptom-resolved network estimation directly from social media discourse and apply the framework to depression and eating disorders, with a third anorexia corpus as cross-dataset validation. To our knowledge, we are the first to estimate symptom-resolved psychometric networks from social media text, compare them to clinical co-endorsement networks, and replicate transdiagnostic linguistic markers across 3 independently recruited corpora spanning 2 disorders simultaneously. For depression, expression scores correlate with BDI-II totals at $ρ{=}0.434$, 20 of 21 items reach FDR significance, and split-half reliability is 0.935. The Network Comparison Test detects few edge differences between modalities (3-5\% of edges), while bridge symptoms diverge. For eating disorders, the item-level results are exploratory. Identified linguistic features replicate the same direction across all 3 corpora, and they cluster in three construct families.

papers.title: Symmetry Detection with Patch Embedding Models by Means of a Scalar Product Transform
papers.abstract: We present a transformation of vector embeddings representing image patches into scores for point reflection symmetry at the crossing points of patches. The transformation is heavily inspired by the Gradient Product Transform, but it uses the vector embeddings instead of the grayscale gradients. We therefore call it the "Scalar Product Transform" (SPT). Unlike deep learning models for symmetry detection, the method does not require a specific training step tailored for symmetry detection, but it works with arbitrary pre-trained patch embedding models. We have tested the method with DINOv3 and Franca. In our tests, the method outperformed the Gradient Product Transform and was even better than EquiSym, a convolutional neural network specifically designed and trained for symmetry detection. Although the runtime of the SPT is greater than that of EquiSym, the SPT has the advantage that it directly yields a bounding box for the symmetric region.

papers.title: A Game of Throngs: How Spotlight Tourism Reshapes Local Economies
papers.abstract: In July 2017, San Juan de Gaztelugatxe, a modest chapel in the Basque Country, appeared as "Dragonstone" in Game of Thrones, transforming a locally known site with limited tourism activity into a global tourist destination overnight. We exploit this exogenous spotlight shock to estimate its causal effects on the local economy using a novel administrative dataset and a Synthetic Control approach. We find an abrupt increase in tourism activity, far exceeding the effects documented in the literature. Despite this surge, employment gains in tourism-related sectors were largely offset by losses elsewhere, resulting in no net effect on total employment. We also document signs of housing-market overheating, with increases in both property transactions and prices. We find no evidence that the shock displaced the local population. Instead, it led to a roughly twofold increase in arrivals from abroad. Taken together, these findings suggest that a substantial increase in tourism activity does not necessarily translate into broad-based local economic gains. Instead, tourism-led growth may entail significant sectoral reallocation and housing-market pressures, underscoring the importance of looking beyond tourism activity alone when assessing its wider economic effects.

papers.title: Exploring the link between predictive uncertainty and the sim-to-real gap in deep learning models utilizing synthetic data
papers.abstract: Today, state-of-the-art methods for quality control (QC) are based on Machine Vision, combining deep learning (DL) models with camera-based inspection. Yet, the integration of such solutions in industrial applications is often impeded by data sparsity and trust in model reliability. While synthetic data offers a promising approach to generate the necessary data with perfect annotations, it poses risks related to performance degradation due to the possible occurrence of the sim-to-real gap. This study conducts experiments using the ensemble method to estimate the predictive uncertainty of DL models trained on synthetic data. The results show that predictive uncertainty increases under the sim-to-real domain shift. However, the observed performance drop is dominated by a systematic sim-to-real bias rather than by ensemble disagreement.These findings contribute to the effective utilization of synthetic data in industrial settings while highlighting the importance of risk assessment for the deployment of DL solutions for QC tasks.

papers.title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
papers.abstract: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction. We construct ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K for two-stage training. Contrastive supervised fine-tuning teaches when and how to respond, while reinforcement learning with Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment (BACA) combines trajectory-level and local advantages to refine decisions, responses, and silence across multi-turn interactions. We also introduce FSI-Bench to evaluate feedback seeking and subsequent task completion. ALIVE achieves the highest overall scores among the compared models on four public benchmarks and FSI-Bench, demonstrating strong streaming understanding and interactive capabilities.

papers.title: Premise Recovery in Software Design: What Does This Decision Rest On?
papers.abstract: Design decisions shape software architecture, and writing them down preserves the reasons behind it. Architecture decision records (ADRs) capture them, each with its context, choice, and consequences. A decision can depend on earlier ones: reversing one of them would force its review. We call these its premises. Yet ADRs do not always name their premises. When a decision is reversed, engineers supersede its ADR and search by hand for what it affects. That search can miss ADRs resting on an unnamed premise. We frame this as premise recovery: given an ADR with identifiers masked, find its premises among earlier records. We collect 1,060 ADRs from 36 repositories and label 1,529 candidate pairs for 60 target ADRs. Two LLM annotators agree at \k{appa} = 0.859. An independent human annotator, blind to their labels, agrees with the stated/implicit tag on 30 of 32 premises (\k{appa} = 0.875). We compare 7 open-weight models with 2 baselines that use no LLM. Qwen3.8-27B reaches F1 0.756, against 0.466 for word overlap; 2 models added post hoc score similarly. On the 11 premises whose titles barely overlap the target, it finds 0.758, while word overlap finds none. Reasoning raises its recall of implicit premises but not its F1. Word overlap with as many predictions gains 69% as much. We find only 2 to 3 stale dependents, though we searched for unlinked ones in only 30 of 66 supersessions. Open models could thus suggest unwritten premises when a decision is reversed, with precision between 0.68 and 0.78.

papers.title: Astrophysical Constraints for Bosonic Dark Matter in and Around Quark Stars
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure, stability, and mass-radius relations of compact stars composed of quark matter within the non-ideal MIT Bag Model mixed with self-interacting bosonic dark matter with a $φ^n$ self-interaction potential. By solving the coupled two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations for boson masses between 200 MeV and 1 GeV and self-interaction strengths with $n=4$ and $n=40$, we show that strong self-interactions and higher boson masses enhance the stability of compact star configurations at high central pressures, though they reduce maximum overall masses. Ultra-compact solutions with $C \ge 1/3$ capable of mimicking black holes are significantly restricted compared to hadronic models, emerging only for strong self-interactions and dark matter fractions exceeding 90\%. Depending on the parameters, the compact stars form either extended dark matter halos or compact cores: stronger self-interactions and higher boson masses suppress the radial extension to favor compact cores of dark matter. Matching our models against observational constraints highlights PSR J1614$-$2230 and XTE J1814$-$338 as potential window of opportunity for dark matter detection. Notably, XTE J1814$-$338 could confirm a dark sector, given its requirement for light boson masses ($m_b \approx 200\text{--}300\text{ MeV}$) and strongly DM-dominated configurations.

papers.title: EP241206a: A Sub-kilosecond X-Ray Flare Possibly from an Active Galactic Nucleus with a Flux Increase over 3 Orders of Magnitude
papers.abstract: EP241206a is a fast X-ray transient detected with the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) on board the Einstein Probe. The event exhibited a single-peaked soft X-ray flare with a duration of $\sim 500$ s and a peak flux of $1.0 \times 10^{-9}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ in 0.5--4 keV, spatially coincident with a spectroscopically confirmed active galactic nucleus (AGN) at $z = 0.62$. Follow-up and archival observations revealed persistent X-ray emission at a level of $\sim 5 \times 10^{-13}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$, corresponding to $L_{2-10 \mathrm{keV}} \simeq 2.3 \times 10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$ if associated with the AGN; the WXT flare reached an estimated peak isotropic-equivalent rest-frame 2--10 keV luminosity of $\sim 1.4 \times 10^{48}$ erg s$^{-1}$, implying a peak-to-persistent luminosity contrast of over 3 orders of magnitude. Optical spectroscopy detected broad Mg II and H$β$ emission lines, suggesting a black hole mass of $\sim 3.8 \times 10^{7} M_{\odot}$ and Eddington ratios of 0.8 at the persistent state versus an apparent peak ratio of $\sim 4.6 \times 10^{3}$ during the flare. The extremely short duration and high apparent peak luminosity favor a jet origin, likely due to magnetic reconnection in the inner regions of a relativistic jet. Alternative scenarios include a jet-in-the-jet or a gamma-ray burst occurring within the AGN disk. However, the physical association between the transient and the AGN is not firmly established; for the radio-loud and X-ray-detected AGN counterpart class, the trial-corrected chance probability is $4.9 \times 10^{-3}$. EP241206a may represent an example of a broader population of unidentified fast X-ray transients detected with WXT.

papers.title: Federated TD Learning in Heterogeneous Environments with Average Rewards: A Two-timescale Approach with Polyak-Ruppert Averaging
papers.abstract: Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL) provides a promising way to speedup training in reinforcement learning when one has access to multiple edge devices that can operate in parallel. Recently, it has been shown that even when these edge devices have access to different dynamic models---such as cars or robots with differing system configurations---an optimal convergence rate that has a linear speedup proportional to the number of devices is achievable. However, this result requires that the algorithm's stepsize be chosen in a manner that depends on the unknown model parameters. Also, it applies only to a discounted setting, which has been argued to fit episodic tasks better than continuing control tasks. In this paper, we obtain finite-time bounds for heterogeneous FRL with average rewards. We show that optimal convergence rate and linear speedup are achievable even with a universal stepsize choice, independent of the underlying dynamics. To achieve our result, we modify the existing one-timescale FRL method to a novel two-timescale variant that additionally incorporates iterate averaging. We remark that this idea also extends to other settings already studied in the literature, such as the homogeneous FRL or the heterogeneous case with a discounted cost function.

papers.title: Information Causality Defeats Every Finite NPA Level
papers.abstract: For every finite level of the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy, we construct correlations that satisfy all its constraints but violate information causality. At each fixed level, one use of a binary-outcome correlation and one classical bit suffice for a violation that grows without bound as the number of measurement settings increases. Information causality bounds the information gained about independent database bits, summed over possible requests, by the length of the message. Quantum correlations obey the one-bit bound; the optimal information gain at any fixed NPA level grows logarithmically with the number of settings. The violation remains unbounded even when all outcome probabilities are positive and, for any fixed number of measurement settings on each side, every choice of those settings admits a local model. One communicated bit therefore exposes an unbounded gap between information causality and every finite NPA level.

papers.title: Learning What Pairs Miss for Higher-Order Multimodal Alignment
papers.abstract: Contrastive learning beyond two modalities now scores the whole tuple with multilinear products, volumes, and fusion heads, critics that can represent the joint distribution. In practice these critics still behave like bags of pairs. Their negatives break at least two of the three pairs, a single pairwise check rejects them, and when most samples can be solved by pairs the higher-order term receives almost no gradient. To solve this problem, we propose CHORD (Contrastive Higher-Order Residuals with Decoys), which trains a residual against decoys drawn from a calibrated pairwise model, negatives that the pairwise model finds plausible, so that rejecting them often needs all three modalities. Drawing decoys costs one inner-product query over a memory bank, and the optimal residual is the log-ratio between the data and the pairwise model, so the decoy loss also bounds what that model misses. On M3-Mix, where one in ten training samples needs all three modalities, our CHORD improves accuracy on those samples by 21.2 percentage points over the strongest of eight baselines. CHORD also gives the best two-to-one results on every real dataset, and its residual improves other retrievers without retraining.

papers.title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. However, current methods primarily depend on single-pass chain-of-thought reasoning that overlooks brief or localized artifacts, or on predefined multi-agent workflows that offer limited flexibility in selecting relevant inspections. Even with adaptive investigation, optimizing the investigation policy alone does not directly improve the forensic capabilities of fixed experts. We introduce WeVisForensics, an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues. The investigator learns which artifact type to examine, over which window, and when to conclude, and these interactions provide shared feedback for both levels of agents. Our dual-timescale policy optimization strategy, DTPO, closes this loop through fast reinforcement learning of the investigator and slower refinement of the inspectors, guided by annotated artifact intervals, to report subtle artifacts they once dismissed. Furthermore, we curate ForenCue-30K, combining role-specific forensic annotations and interaction trajectories to supervise individual inspections and their coordination, with an accompanying reinforcement-learning pool. Experiments show that WeVisForensics averages 95.2% detection accuracy across in-domain, out-of-domain and agentic benchmarks, 9.0% above the strongest prior detector, while grounding its verdicts in localized evidence.

papers.title: An improved weighted broad $L^2$ estimate in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For a compact smooth plane curve $S$ with nonzero curvature and a union $X\subseteq B_R$ of unit balls satisfying a one-dimensional Katz--Tao condition, we prove $\|\mathrm{Br}_A E_S f\|_{L^2(X)} \leq C_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'} R^{\varepsilon}|X|^{13/62}\|f\|_2$. The proof relies on a refined local broad estimate that uses density decomposition and the short frequency intervals associated with coarse tubes.

papers.title: Proceedings Eighth International Workshop on Formal Methods for Autonomous Systems
papers.abstract: This EPTCS volume contains the papers from the Eighth International Workshop on Formal Methods for Autonomous Systems (FMAS 2026), which was held on the 17th and 18th of November 2026. FMAS 2026 was co-located with the 27th International Conference on Formal Engineering Methods (ICFEM), and hosted at the Leonardo Royal Grand Harbour Hotel in Southampton.

papers.title: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
papers.abstract: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment. However, as people increasingly employ autonomous, LLM-powered AI agents that make decisions on their behalf in doing day-to-day tasks, it is of critical importance that we understand how implicit biases, based on sociodemographic assumptions, emerge across a broad milieu of workaday decision scenarios. We used the 17 domains of daily activity in the American Time Use Survey (ATUS) to generate an atlas of 506 decision scenarios in which LLMs --- endowed with personas representing different races, gender identities, and political ideologies --- expressed significant implicit bias. Next, in a crowdsourced audit, 500 participants made 8,010 binary choices about which implicitly biased decision scenarios most deserved further review. We found that participants prioritized decision scenarios that had broad relevance (e.g., about food choices), were high stakes (e.g., about health), and where all members of a simulated sociodemographic group made unanimous decisions (because it was a clear indication of stereotyping). They were less swayed by the magnitude of an observed disparity or the specific ATUS domain the decision scenario represented. When examining the rationale behind their prioritization choices, we found that participants often interpreted disparities as traits of demographic groups and judged whether those traits seemed plausible, often based on their own internalized stereotypes. We discuss implications for building personalized AI agents, digital twins, social simulations, and for using crowdsourced bias audits.

papers.title: Douglas--Rachford Algorithm with Relaxed Resolvents
papers.abstract: The Douglas--Rachford algorithm is a classical method for finding a zero of the sum of two maximally monotone operators. In its standard form, both operators are reflected in the same manner and are activated with the same step-size. In this article we break this symmetry by replacing the reflected resolvents by relaxed resolvents, letting the two operators be activated with different step-sizes. We show that this additional freedom is available precisely when the operators are cocoercive, the admissible range of the parameter being determined by their cocoercivity constants and reducing to the classical algorithm when these constants vanish. Within this range we quantify the averagedness of the resulting operator, which yields the weak convergence of the method together with relaxation steps beyond those allowed in the classical case, and, when one of the operators is in addition strongly monotone, a strict contraction. We compute in closed form the parameters minimizing the contraction factor and we exhibit instances attaining it, so that the resulting linear rates are tight. The optimal rates are strictly smaller than the best rates available for the classical Douglas--Rachford algorithm in the monotone inclusion and convex optimization settings, which are studied separately. All theoretical rates are corroborated by the numerical worst cases obtained via performance estimation.

papers.title: Data-Driven Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Racing under Varying Friction
papers.abstract: Data-driven predictive control (DPC) predicts future outputs by combining recorded input-output trajectory data such that the combined trajectory approximately matches a measured initial trajectory and tracks a provided reference. This paper investigates to what extent and under which conditions DPC using data pooled across operating conditions retains the prediction accuracy of DPC using data from the current operating condition. In autonomous vehicle racing, the tire-road friction varies between racetrack sections and tire sets. If the initial trajectory and the recorded data originate from different frictions, prediction accuracy of DPC degrades. Ensuring the frictions match requires knowing the friction during recording and estimating the current friction explicitly. Instead, we pool data recorded at different frictions. We compare the prediction accuracy of DPC using data recorded under the current friction (matched), a different friction (mismatched) and data pooled from both frictions. We evaluate in simulation and small-scale vehicle experiments in the Cyber-Physical Mobility Lab (CPM Lab). Our results show that pooled data keep the multi-step root-mean-square prediction error within 1.5 times that of matched data, whereas mismatched data increase it by a factor of 2.2 to 3.4. To assess how this prediction accuracy carries over to control, we evaluate the tracking error from the raceline in closed loop. In simulation, DPC with pooled data tracks comparably to nonlinear model predictive control (13.7 cm versus 13.3 cm) and close to DPC with matched data in the CPM Lab, differing by 0.1 cm on the low-friction tires (1.6 cm versus 1.5 cm) and by 0.2 cm on the high-friction tires (0.9 cm versus 1.1 cm). DPC thus provides partial adaptation to varying friction, without a dedicated adaptation method.

papers.title: What's the Difference? Voice Design and Confirmation Bias in AI-Assisted Self-Diagnosis: Anthropomorphic vs. Machine-Like Voice Output
papers.abstract: As symptom checkers based on artificial intelligence (AI) are becoming common entry points for health information, their influence on lay users' diagnostic decisions raises questions about trust and bias. Of particular concern is confirmation bias, the tendency to favour information that supports one's existing belief while discounting information that contradicts it. One of the central design choices for such systems is the style of voice: whether they should present themselves with a human-like (anthropomorphic) or a clearly machine-like (xenomorphic) voice. This study investigates whether the voice design of an AI symptom checker modulates confirmation bias in self-diagnosis. In a within-subjects online experiment (N = 81 participants, 648 trials), participants selected a diagnosis and rated their confidence, then heard an AI-generated recommendation that either confirmed or contradicted their initial choice, delivered by an anthropomorphic or a machine-like voice, before deciding again. We observed a strong, direction-dependent influence of the AI: participants revised their diagnosis in 45.7% of trials when the AI contradicted them versus 1.2% when it confirmed them (generalised linear mixed model, GLMM, p < .001); confidence rose under confirmation but barely moved under contradiction (robust linear mixed model, p < .001); and decisions took longer after contradiction (Gamma GLMM, p < .001). This effect did not differ between the two voices (no voice or interaction term was significant, smallest p = .282), even though a manipulation check confirmed the voices were perceived as markedly different. The findings suggest that the direction of an AI recommendation, rather than the anthropomorphism of its voice, drives confirmation-related bias in AI-assisted self-diagnosis.

papers.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
papers.abstract: We introduce EJBench, a benchmark of engineering judgement: whether a model can predict how a design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier results, and decide on it. Unlike engineering benchmarks that test whether an agent can operate simulation or CAD software, EJBench is software-agnostic and asks what an engineer would conclude without running a simulation. Its tasks come from a conjugate heat transfer design campaign for battery cold plates, in three families: matching unlabelled test results to their operating points, choosing which stored runs to reveal before signing off a design, and ranking new duties by peak cell temperature. Every answer is taken from a converged simulation, not from an LLM judge. The best of ten frontier models, GPT-6 Astra, scores 0.71, and models state almost the same confidence on tasks they get wrong as on tasks they get right. We also post-train Qwen3.5-9B with LoRA and reinforcement learning, rewarded by the share of answer criteria the simulation results confirm; on the held-out test split its score rises from 0.071 to 0.106. We release the train, validation and test splits, the evaluation harness and the leaderboard.

papers.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.

papers.title: Multilevel AlScN Ferroelectric Diode Crossbar Arrays with Sub-200 nm Cells for Selector-Free Nonvolatile Memory
papers.abstract: Passive crossbar arrays are a leading route to high-density nonvolatile memory and in-memory computing, but without a selector the memory element itself must supply the nonlinearity that suppresses sneak-path currents. Here we scale aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric diodes (FeDs) in both dimensions that matter - the ferroelectric is thinned to 10 nm and the junction diameter is reduced to 100 nm. We further integrate 200 nm cells into a 2-kilobyte (128 * 128) passive crossbar. At a junction area of 0.0314 um2 this is a ~625 reduction in cell area, at equal array capacity, relative to kilobyte-scale AlScN FeD crossbars built on 5 μm cells. The 10 nm Al0.64Sc0.36N layer reverses its polarization under pulses of 50 ns full width at half maximum at a pulse-energy density of ~16 pJ μm-2, corresponding to ~0.5 pJ per 200 nm cell. Pulsed programming at 17.5 V and 1 kHz yields an ON/OFF ratio of 4.2 * 103 in a 200 nm cell, while DC characterization of 283 randomly addressed cells of the 2-kB array gives ON/OFF and rectification ratios at 5 V of 43 33 and 61 74, from which we derive the sub-array size that selector-free reading currently supports. Eight conductance levels (three bits) written into a 200 nm array cell remain resolvable for 103 s, and the two extreme states are stable beyond 5 * 104 s. Mapping the measured, nonuniformly spaced levels onto a ResNet-20 network recovers 91.7 +- 0.1 % CIFAR-10 accuracy after quantization-aware training, against a 92.2 +- 0.1 % full-precision baseline. AlScN FeDs thus combine nanosecond switching, three-bit storage and sub-0.05 μm2 cells in a BEOL-compatible, selector-free crossbar.

papers.title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
papers.abstract: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium. We introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0 (VAS), a benchmark of 211 creation and modification tasks spanning presentations, static graphics, animations and videos, and web interfaces. Each task specifies authoring objectives, source materials, constraints, and deliverables. Existing benchmarks provide limited support for systematically evaluating how authoring choices suit different audiences, purposes, and media across artifact families. VAS evaluates two aspects separately: Task Fulfillment verifies explicit requirements and applicable functionality, while Artifact Performance assesses Content, Organization, Visuals, and Delivery. Task-specific rating anchors instantiate shared criteria for the intended audience, purpose, and medium, with judgments grounded in source materials and artifact inspection records. We evaluate nine model-harness configurations on all 211 tasks. Overall scores range from 42.12 to 70.52, with Artifact Performance accounting for 73.4% of the gap between the highest- and lowest-scoring configurations.

papers.title: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. This mismatch can produce accurate rendered masks from incomplete 3D selections since alpha-blended feature supervision concentrates learning on dominant contributors while leaving occluded or low-contribution Gaussians weakly supervised. We propose VODA, a plug-and-play supervision objective that exploits local depth structure to group per-pixel contributors and directly supervises all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, bypassing contribution-weighted gradient delivery. To evaluate volumetric completeness, we introduce Removal-3D, a synthetic object-removal benchmark, and the Removal Depth Error (RDE), a metric comparing predicted and ground-truth depth changes. Across four rendering-based baselines, VODA consistently improves volumetric segmentation on Removal-3D while maintaining or improving performance on LERF and ScanNet. Further analysis shows that VODA recovers lower-contribution Gaussians, while simple gradient reweighting and spatial propagation fail to reproduce comparable gains.

papers.title: Stability-Compensated Threshold Calibration for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models often produce hallucinated answers, motivating selective prediction policies that abstain on uncertain queries. However, heuristic uncertainty thresholds alone do not provide statistical control of errors among accepted predictions. Linear Expectation Constraints (LEC) reduce selection-conditioned error rate (SCER) calibration to a nonpositive expected linear-loss constraint, but the associated loss is non-monotonic in the acceptance threshold. We construct an exact counterexample under i.i.d. sampling demonstrating that LEC's empirical threshold-selection rule can violate the population SCER target. To address this risk-transfer gap, we introduce Stability-Compensated Linear Expectation Control (SC-LEC), which uses the negative linear risk of a theoretical full-data reference to compensate for threshold-selection instability. For local expansion beyond a safe anchor, we derive two finite-sample certificates: a stability-based certificate exploiting rank crossings and a direct certificate using the structure of threshold expansion to reduce conservatism. With a valid population anchor margin, our certificate conditions ensure finite-sample marginal SCER control, and independent margin certification further provides a $1-δ$ high-probability guarantee for this calibration-averaged control. Experiments on CommonsenseQA, ARC-Challenge, and TriviaQA show useful retention gains beyond the same certified anchor, while revealing conservative behavior in small-margin regimes.

papers.title: \(A_α\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
papers.abstract: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_α(G)=αD(G)+(1-α)A(G)\) for \(0\leqα<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_α\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_α(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters. These sets contain no rational parameters other than \(0\) and \(1/2\), for which the adjacency and signless Laplacian cases are characterized by gcd criteria. For even-order paths rooted at either central vertex, we explicitly evaluate the root resultant and the walk-determinant polynomial in the rooted-product factorization. The resulting controllability criterion combines \(A_α\)-controllability of the base graph with at most three explicit spectral exclusions. For each parameter, one of two fixed complementary base graphs yields controllable products for every even-order path and both central roots. For \(1/2\leqα<1\), algebraic conjugates further simplify the spectral test for general rooted products.

papers.title: Continuous superradiant lasing on a narrow optical transition
papers.abstract: Lasers with ultrastable frequency are at the foundation of optical clocks, which enable precision tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy at the centimetre scale. Such lasers inherit their frequency stability from the length stability of a sophisticated optical resonator, which is hard to maintain outside a well-controlled laboratory environment and limited by thermal and technical noise. Superradiant lasers promise to overcome these limitations by storing their coherence in the atoms making up the laser's gain medium. Superradiant lasing has been demonstrated on narrow optical atomic transitions with pulsed and quasi-continuous operation. However, atom loss has prevented truly continuous operation, which severely limits their suitability for clocks. Here we demonstrate a superradiant laser on a narrow optical transition in $^{88}$Sr that operates truly continuously. We sustain emission for more than eight hours and measure a linewidth of 320(40) Hz, more than 20 times below the natural linewidth. The emission frequency remains anchored to the atomic transition, making the laser itself an atomic frequency reference. Our results provide a route towards a laser that reaches short-term frequency stability comparable to that of the best resonator-stabilized lasers. Furthermore, truly continuous operation gives us access to physics beyond the transient regime, enabling the exploration of robust nonequilibrium steady states and sustained coherent collective dynamics.

papers.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Constant-Factor EFX Allocations of Chores
papers.abstract: We study the fair division of indivisible chores among agents with additive disutilities, focusing on the central fairness notion of envy-freeness up to any chore (EFX), and its multiplicative approximations. Although the existence of constant-factor approximations to EFX are known, computing such an allocation in polynomial time remained open. We resolve this question by giving an algorithm that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, computes a $(3+\varepsilon)$-EFX allocation in time polynomial in the input length and $1/\varepsilon$. Our result relies on two algorithmic contributions. First, we give a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for earning-restricted (ER) equilibria with equal earning requirements and arbitrary feasible chore earning limits. We develop a new nonconvex program with chore payouts and money-flow variables, and prove that every local maximum yields an exact ER equilibrium. We then give a mirror-ascent algorithm for this program and prove that it converges to an approximate ER equilibrium in polynomial time. Second, we give a new procedure that converts the approximate equilibrium into a $(3+\varepsilon)$-EFX-friendly allocation, a suitable starting point for the chore-swap framework of Garg and Murhekar (2026). The procedure uses a flexible price threshold to choose swap chores and their recipients together, overcoming a factor-four bottleneck in the earlier approaches while accommodating approximate earnings. We expect these ideas to be useful more broadly in fair division, including for goods and other fairness notions.

papers.title: Carroll Double Copy
papers.abstract: We construct a double copy for Carroll gravity as the ``square'' of Carroll Yang-Mills theory at the linearised level. Starting from the convolutional double copy prescription in Lorentzian spacetime, we take the Carrollian limit $c \rightarrow 0$ to establish a double copy dictionary compatible both with symmetries and the corresponding equations of motion. Since this limit yields two distinct sectors, namely the electric and magnetic Carroll theories, we systematically investigate double copy constructions involving all possible combinations of these parent theories. To accommodate the time-independent on-shell configurations of the magnetic Carroll fields, we introduce a suitable regularisation procedure for the convolutional double copy. In addition, the covariance of the double copy under Carroll boosts requires an appropriate dressing of the fields, leading to the inclusion of a Goldstone-type object in the construction. We first develop the formalism using toy models involving scalar fields and then apply it to the double copy between linearised Carroll Yang-Mills theory and Carroll gravity.

papers.title: Vanishing Relative Distance of Uniformly Random CSS LDPC Codes Built from Permutation Matrices
papers.abstract: Classical random regular low-density parity-check codes can have minimum distance growing linearly with block length. We study CSS check matrices formed as full $J\times L$ arrays of arbitrary $P\times P$ permutation matrices, sampled uniformly subject to commutation. For fixed column weight $J\ge3$ and fixed even row weight $L>2J$, we prove that the relative minimum distance converges to zero in probability as $P\to\infty$, with block length $n=LP$. We analyze the weight enumerators that count all nontrivial logical representatives after excluding stabilizers. A coefficientwise lower bound shows that, at every fixed relative weight $0<α<1$ along even-weight sequences, exponentially many such representatives exist with high probability. Their typical and mean counts have exponent lower bound $h_2(α)/2$, where $h_2$ is the binary entropy function. We compare this bound with the classical LDPC and dense CSS mean weight-distribution exponents. The existence, with high probability, of a logical operator below every fixed target weight $δn$ yields the distance conclusion.

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: Nonparametric Instrumental Kernel Regression: The Well- and Misspecified Setting Under General Link Conditions
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric instrumental variable regression when the outcome takes values in a separable Hilbert space $\mathbb{Y}$, for instance a curve, a density or the kernel mean embedding of a distribution. The structural function solves an ill-posed operator equation whose conditional expectation operator need not be injective, and whose solutions need not belong to the hypothesis space. We analyse a two-stage kernel estimator that extends kernel instrumental variable regression to $\mathbb{Y}$-valued outcomes and allows spectral regularisation in both stages, including Landweber iteration and Showalter's method in the second stage. We show that the second stage is a regularisation method in the Hilbert scale generated by the inverse of the kernel integral operator.
